agent.problem: The opening card introduces an unnamed singer and his need, but it never says whom he is addressing. Looking 'UP' hints at a direction without identifying the LORD as the one being spoken to.

rule.text: It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

agent.problem: The earlier cards establish waiting and repeated requests for mercy, but give no clue to what the people have endured. Hunger and sickness are just as plausible as contempt, so the baker can only guess at wording that has not yet been shown.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: No earlier card identifies who is treating the people with scorn. The preceding answer supplies only 'contempt,' which does not distinguish the arrogant from nations or rulers, making this another guess at an unseen word rather than an inference supported by the setup.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: The quoted punchline adds several separate sentences after the setup: 'That truck was RIGHT THERE.' 'Friend.' 'RIGHT.' 'THERE.' This puts the story card well past the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

agent.problem: Card 6 says only that David is starting a new picture and gives no water imagery or other distinguishing context. Fires and winds can also be described as raging, so filling in 'waters' depends on guessing the wording of a line the baker has not seen.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
